reader.summary: The week was dominated by the final days of the US midterm election campaign, with polls closing November 3. President Trump campaigned aggressively but cancelled in-person rallies in Kansas and Iowa in favor of telerallies, and he demanded the Alaska Democratic Senate candidate be removed from the ballot. A federal judge ordered the administration to stop threatening election officials with prosecution. Pope Leo XIV made history as the first pope ever to vote in a US general election. In a major diplomatic development, Flavio Bolsonaro fled Brazil after losing the presidential election and landed in Florida, where Trump said he could stay 'as long as he wants.' The US-Iran conflict continued, with Trump declaring the war would end 'when I want it to' while warning Gulf allies to prepare for possible strikes after the midterms; costs reportedly ballooned to $47 billion. The US economy posted 3.4 percent growth, the fastest in a year, though inflation remained stubbornly high, and the Fed held rates steady. Washington approved a $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine. Trump's lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal over Epstein reporting was dismissed yet again. Pioneering labor leader Dolores Huerta died at 96.

developments.subject: US Midterm Elections
developments.what_happened: The final week of the midterm campaign saw Trump cancel in-person rallies in favor of telerallies, demand the Alaska Democrat be removed from the ballot, and a judge order the administration to stop threatening election officials, while Pope Leo XIV voted for the first time in a US general election.

developments.subject: US-Iran War and Post-Election Strike Warnings
developments.what_happened: Trump declared the Iran war would end 'when I want it to' while the US warned Gulf allies to prepare for possible strikes after the midterms; Iran targeted US air defenses at Mideast bases, and war costs reportedly reached $47 billion.

developments.subject: Flavio Bolsonaro Flees to US
developments.what_happened: Flavio Bolsonaro fled Brazil after losing the presidential election, landed in Florida, and was granted a US visa; Trump said he could stay 'as long as he wants,' while Rubio insisted the US did not facilitate the flight, and Bolsonaro declared himself Brazil's 'leader' in exile.

developments.subject: US Economy and Fed
developments.what_happened: The US economy posted 3.4 percent growth, the fastest in a year, but inflation remained stubbornly high; the Fed held rates steady ahead of the elections, and AI spending nearing $1 trillion alongside Alphabet's sales miss rattled tech stocks.

developments.subject: Trump's Legal Battles and Court Rulings
developments.what_happened: A judge dismissed Trump's lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal over Epstein reporting for a third time, ordered the administration to stop threatening election officials, pushed back on the DC arch 'national security' argument, and ruled the DOJ unlawfully fired Epstein prosecutor Maurene Comey.

developments.subject: Alaska Senate Race
developments.what_happened: Trump demanded the Alaska Democratic Senate candidate be removed from the ballot after a New York Times report, the administration accelerated a criminal probe into the race, and Alaska attorneys called the demand 'meritless' and 'not even possible.'

developments.subject: Ukraine Defense and Patriot Sale
developments.what_happened: The US approved a $2.1 billion sale of Patriot interceptors to Ukraine after an alleged holdup, and Ukraine paused strikes on Russian refineries after pressure from Washington.

developments.subject: US-Cuba Tensions
developments.what_happened: The US kicked out a Cuban diplomat after a heated exchange at the UN, and the UN adopted a resolution demanding the end of the US embargo on Cuba.

developments.subject: Afghan Deportations
developments.what_happened: Documents showed the US planned to deport Afghan immigrants back to Afghanistan through Pakistan, drawing criticism as part of the administration's immigration enforcement.

developments.subject: US-China Relations
developments.what_happened: China made its first inquiry for US wheat since the Trump-Xi summit, the US planned to ban Chinese telecom firms from direct access to US phone numbers, and China-linked spam accounts were found posing as US voters on X.

developments.subject: Dolores Huerta's Death
developments.what_happened: Pioneering US labor and civil rights leader Dolores Huerta died at age 96, marking the loss of a major figure in American labor history.

display.headline: Midterm Upset and Iran Strikes Define Volatile Week
emoji_reasons: The November 3 midterm election is the defining event of the week with results and disputes dominating.
The US-Iran conflict will see post-election strikes and retaliatory action in the Gulf region.
Flavio Bolsonaro's flight to the US and his exile status will add a major diplomatic story.
display.tldr: The November 3 midterms will produce a contentious result with legal challenges, and the US will follow through on warned strikes against Iran. Bolsonaro's arrival in Florida will add a new diplomatic headache.
display.eli5:
Next week is basically the biggest week of the US political year. On November 3, Americans will vote in the midterm elections, and based on how tense things are right now, the results will probably be super close and disputed. The president has already been making legal moves in Alaska and California, so expect court fights to follow the vote.

At the same time, the US and Iran are in a standoff. The US has told countries around the Gulf to get ready for possible strikes after the election. If those strikes happen, Iran will hit back at US bases or ships, and the whole region will be on edge.

There is also a big new story: Flavio Bolsonaro, who lost the Brazilian presidential election, has fled to Florida. He is calling himself Brazil's leader in exile, and Trump is basically saying he can stay as long as he wants. That is creating a lot of awkwardness for US diplomats.

A surprise would be if the US and Russia suddenly announce some kind of sanctions deal, which would catch everyone off guard given how tense things are between the two countries.

Sign: A headline about a new poll in a contested state showing a narrow margin, paired with a candidate speech addressing the cost of living and foreign-policy fallout.

Tehran will respond with retaliatory measures against US assets in the Gulf, forcing the White House to justify its military posture before the midterms. The Alaska Senate certification lawsuit will reach a critical legal milestone as a federal judge rules on the Justice Department motion, sharpening the partisan fight over election integrity. The midterm campaign will enter its final stretch with consumer sentiment near record lows and heating oil costs becoming a defining issue for Republican candidates. Ukraine diplomacy will see last-minute positioning ahead of the planned three-way talks in Abu Dhabi, while the DeepSeek ban and F-35 purchase will recede from the headlines.
